done_when: forge sync refreshes generated files while other items' work or land runs, and waits for or skips only what that run actually holds, saying so in one line

findings.body: Raise: Data loss. During an upgrade, an earlier-release `forge work` run can hold this lock, causing sync to skip its chat and say the run will keep it. The v1.2.2 worker takes the same lock (`tests/fixtures/forge-v1.2.2/src/forge/worker.py:80`) but commits only status (`:116`); it never commits the chat binding. Upgrade invokes sync once (`src/forge/upgrade.py:163-165`), so when that worker finishes, the chat remains only in `.git/forge` and is lost if the local record disappears or work moves to another machine. The named proof holds a current-release worker after running the old release sequentially, so it does not catch this case.
findings.title: Old-release runs leave skipped chats only in local records

why: forge sync refuses whenever any other item's forge work or land is running on the machine, so workers copy the guide by hand
